name: Nucleus of the solitary tract
summary: The visceral sensory nucleus of the brainstem. It surrounds the solitary tract in the dorsolateral medulla and receives taste from the anterior tongue (via the facial nerve), the posterior tongue (glossopharyngeal) and the epiglottis (vagus) in its rostral part, and general visceral afferents from the carotid sinus and body, the aortic arch, the heart, lungs and gut in its caudal part. It is the sensory hub for the baroreceptor, chemoreceptor, cough, gag and vomiting reflexes.

anatomy.location: Dorsolateral medulla lateral to the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus and ventral to the vestibular nuclei, running from the caudal pons to the obex where the two sides fuse into the commissural nucleus.

function: First central relay for taste and for visceral afferent information; drives cardiovascular and respiratory reflexes through projections to the ventrolateral medulla, the dorsal vagal nucleus and the nucleus ambiguus, and sends taste to the ventral posteromedial thalamus.

bestView.label: dorsolateral medulla medial to the inferior cerebellar peduncle
dorsal medulla beneath the vestibular area

imaging.normalAppearance: Not visible on routine MRI; its position is the dorsolateral medulla just beneath the floor of the fourth ventricle. Lesions here belong to the dorsolateral medullary infarct pattern.

pathology.finding: Dorsolateral medullary restricted diffusion; baroreflex failure and labile blood pressure may accompany the classical signs.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: DWI; autonomic testing when blood pressure is unstable

lesionEffects.deficit: Loss of taste on the ipsilateral tongue
lesionEffects.mechanism: Gustatory part of the nucleus or the solitary tract

lesionEffects.deficit: Baroreflex failure with labile hypertension and tachycardia
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of carotid sinus and aortic arch afferent processing

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired gag, cough and swallowing reflexes

examination: Taste testing with sugar and salt on each side of the tongue
Orthostatic blood pressure and heart rate
pearls: Taste from all three cranial nerves converges here, so a single medullary lesion can abolish taste on the whole ipsilateral tongue
Baroreflex failure after brainstem stroke or radiotherapy presents with wild blood pressure swings
